property_summary: After one call to play() with player sending 10 wei, pot becomes 0 on the correct contract but remains 10 on the buggy contract.

After two consecutive calls to play() with the same player sending 10 wei each time, with a random outcome of 0 on the second call (ensuring pot is 10 before payout), the reference sets pot to 0 after payout, while the buggy version leaves pot at 10.

After a single call to play() that results in random == 0 (using block.timestamp and block.difficulty to force that outcome), the reference contract sets pot to 0, while the buggy contract leaves pot as 10.
After a player calls play() with 10 wei and random(block.timestamp, block.difficulty) % 2 == 0, the pot becomes 0 on the reference but remains 10 on the buggy contract.
After one play() call where random == 0, the reference sets pot to 0 while the buggy version leaves pot as 10.

When a user calls play() with 10 wei, in the reference (random==0) the user receives pot-1 (9 wei) and bank gets 1 wei, while in the mutant (random==1) the user keeps their 10 wei (pot is not distributed) and bank gets nothing.

After two calls by different users, the reference distributes the pot on the second call (random == 0) leaving bank with 1 wei and user2 with 19 wei, while the bug (random == 1) does not distribute, so user2's balance remains 0 and bank unchanged.

After one play call, the reference distributes the pot to the player if random == 0, while the bug distributes only if random == 1, so using vm.warp to fix block.timestamp to a value that makes random == 0 in the reference, the reference causes the bank to receive 1 wei (and pot becomes 0), while the bug leaves bank unchanged.

After two play() calls with 10 wei each, when the second call's random value is 0 (reference) or 1 (mutant), the reference distributes the pot (user2 receives 19 wei, bank receives 1 wei) while the mutant does not distribute (user2 receives nothing, bank receives nothing).
